towers.name: A timeline of towers to scale

data.text: Two thousand years of lighthouses, to one scale

towers.name: Pharos
towers.story: One of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world, a fire on its top guiding ships into the harbour; brought down by earthquakes in the 1300s.

towers.name: Hercules
towers.story: Built by the Romans on a headland in north-west Spain and still lit today: the oldest lighthouse in use.

towers.name: Smeaton's
towers.story: Of the two wooden towers before it, one was swept away by a storm and one burned down. Smeaton built in dovetailed granite, shaped like an oak — every stone tower after learned from it.

towers.name: Bell Rock
towers.story: Built on a reef that drowns at high tide, the men working only at low water; today the oldest surviving sea-washed lighthouse.

towers.name: Cordouan
towers.story: Called the Versailles of the sea. In 1823 the world's first Fresnel lens was lit here.

towers.name: Skerryvore
towers.story: Six years' work by Alan Stevenson on an Atlantic reef: the tallest lighthouse in Scotland.

towers.name: S. Foreland
towers.story: The first lighthouse lit by electricity, in trials overseen by Michael Faraday.

towers.name: Île Vierge
towers.story: At 82.5 metres the tallest stone lighthouse in the world: 365 steps to the top.

towers.name: Jeddah
towers.story: A slender tower of reinforced concrete, 133 metres: the tallest lighthouse in the world.

towers.name: N. Foreland
towers.story: The last staffed lighthouse in Britain went automatic. The last keepers came down, and the light shone on.

brief.subject: The history of the lighthouse
brief.intent: From a fire on a tower to the automatic light, what each step changed; and how tall they were, side by side
brief.audience: Anyone who likes history and buildings
brief.concept: Ten real lighthouses standing along a line of years, all drawn to one scale against a ruler of metres — a timeline that is also a comparison of heights. Pick one to hear what it left to the story.
brief.direction: Like a museum panel: warm white, fine ink, the stones in their own colours, the accent only for the one being told

basis.intent: how they came to be what they are
